provenance.summary: Provisional fixture curves. Every damage fraction below is ASSUMED. No curve here is measured, calibrated or validated against loss experience.
provenance.baseline_derivation: Baseline pre-FBC fractions are the platform's already-published vulnerability assumption (risk.wind_damage_ratio: min(0.85, 0.9 * ((kt - 50) / 100) ** 2.2), sustained knots) evaluated on this file's gust grid using kt = mph / (1.15078 * 1.30). Reusing it keeps one vulnerability assumption in the product rather than two competing ones.
provenance.upgrade_derivation: Upgrade curves are the baseline scaled by (1 - effectiveness) using the hurricane effectiveness already published on /api/meta/model: opening-protection 0.25 for 'shutters', roof-to-wall 0.20 for 'roof_straps'. This is an assumed uniform effect across all wind speeds, which is almost certainly wrong in shape: real mitigation effects vary with intensity.
provenance.code_uplift_derivation: post_fbc_2002 baseline is pre_fbc_2002 scaled by 0.60, an assumed uplift for homes built to the 2002 Florida Building Code. Not sourced.
provenance.finance_workbook_status: StormShield_Finance_Data_v5.xlsx returned NO damage-effect evidence: 'Data Request - Upgrades' tables A and B have every Answer cell blank ('—'), under an explicit ground rule that a premium discount must not be converted into a damage reduction. These fixtures exist so the engine can run before that request is answered; they are not a substitute for it.
provenance.do_not: Do not present these as FORTIFIED, IBHS or study-derived results. Replace this whole file when the math/research team supplies curves.

curves.source_note: Assumed. Platform vulnerability curve risk.wind_damage_ratio on the gust grid. Single-family home built before the 2002 Florida Building Code.

Assumed. Baseline x 0.75 (opening-protection hurricane effectiveness 0.25). Scope: whole-house accordion shutters on every opening, per Finance workbook row 'Hurricane shutters — accordion, whole-house'.

Assumed. Baseline x 0.80 (roof-to-wall hurricane effectiveness 0.20). Scope: roof-to-wall strap/clip retrofit on an existing roof. Finance workbook flags the sourced price at $850-$5,000, not the $20,000 the starter model assumed.
Assumed. pre_fbc_2002 baseline x 0.60 code-uplift factor. Single-family home built to the 2002 Florida Building Code or later.

Assumed. post_fbc_2002 baseline x 0.75. No roof_straps curve exists for this class: roof-to-wall connections are already required by the 2002 code, so the retrofit is not an eligible option and must not be offered.
